diagnosis.root_cause: Marginal customer fibre path with degraded, oscillating RX power causing repeated optical disconnects and re-authentication. The ONT laser, shared PON infrastructure, router, VLAN, and RADIUS records are healthy.
evidence: The customer's current RX power is -27.94 dBm, in the degraded band and close to critical; the telemetry repeatedly swings between degraded and critical levels.
The seven-day RX series starts in the degraded band rather than the normal band, so this is not a declining-link diagnosis under the stated rule.
RX oscillation with 16 sessions in 24 hours meets the 8+ flapping threshold, and the average session duration of 71 minutes is far below the 11.9-hour network mean.
TX power remains normal around +2.3 dBm, TX bias current is stable within the healthy range, and distance remains constant at 302 m; this rules out laser degradation and distance change.
All tested peers on EPON0/2 are online with materially better RX levels, so the fault is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON port or splitter.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, and temperature, and all seven tested PONs are healthy; this rules out an OLT or shared infrastructure failure.
The ONU is currently online and responding, so there is no current ONU-offline fault.

RADIUS exists and is CRM-consistent, the VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1092, the router heartbeat is healthy, and traffic is present; authentication, VLAN, router, and service-provisioning faults are not supported.

remediation.action: Dispatch field service to inspect and clean the customer drop, connectors, splice points, and splitter path; measure end-to-end optical loss and repair or replace the degraded fibre path as necessary. Monitor RX power and session count after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: RX power oscillates between roughly -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle, crossing the threshold at which the link stops being usable. The session drops follow the signal excursions.
expected_reasoning: Sixteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 71 minute mean duration
Cached RX is -26.28 dBm, already in the degraded band
Telemetry shows RX oscillating between about -24.4 and -28.2 dBm on an eleven hour cycle
The lower excursions cross -28 dBm, at which point the link becomes unusable
Live RX of -27.94 confirms the signal is currently near the bottom of that swing
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable, so the ONU is healthy
RADIUS is clean with a single consistent entry and no mismatches
Peers on EPON0/2 read normal, so the fault is in this customer's own path
The session pattern tracks the signal excursions, so the optical fault explains the flapping
distractors: The trigger names the session count, pointing at the auth layer
Sixteen disconnects is well within the observed flapping tail and could be read as a CPE fault
